summary.en: A free six-week residential programme at MIT for US high-school juniors: five rigorous courses in maths, science and humanities, lab tours and admissions coaching. Tuition, room and board are all covered.
summary.ka: უფასო ექვსკვირიანი პროგრამა MIT-ის კამპუსზე აშშ-ის მე-11 კლასელებისთვის: ხუთი ინტენსიური კურსი მათემატიკაში, მეცნიერებასა და ჰუმანიტარულ საგნებში, ლაბორატორიების ტურები და მისაღები კონსულტაციები. სწავლა, საცხოვრებელი და კვება სრულად დაფარულია.
summary.ar: برنامج إقامة مجاني لستة أسابيع في MIT لطلاب الصف الحادي عشر الأمريكيين: خمس مواد مكثفة في الرياضيات والعلوم والإنسانيات وجولات في المختبرات وإرشاد للقبول الجامعي. الدراسة والسكن والطعام مغطاة بالكامل.

about.en:
MITES Summer is MIT's flagship six-week residential STEM programme for rising high-school seniors. Around 80 students live in MIT dormitories and take five courses (typically a maths course, a physics or life-science course, a humanities course, and project-based electives such as engineering design or computer science) taught by MIT-affiliated instructors, with recitations, workshops, lab tours and a written evaluation from each instructor at the end.

The programme targets talented students from communities under-represented in science and engineering, including first-generation, low-income and rural students. Classes run weekdays 9:00 to 17:00; evenings and weekends bring social events and trips around Greater Boston, plus college-admissions counselling.

It is entirely free: MIT and its donors cover tuition, housing and meals, and students pay only travel to and from campus. Admission is very competitive and is a strong signal on university applications. Note: only US citizens and permanent residents are eligible; international students should look at other programmes in this list.

en: Completely free six weeks on MIT's campus, including room and board
Five college-level courses plus admissions counselling and written instructor evaluations
Strong alumni network: many MITES alumni go on to MIT and other top universities

eligibility.en: US citizens or permanent residents (green card) in 11th grade at the time of application; public, private and home-schooled students welcome. Students may not apply from outside the US. Priority is given to students from under-represented and under-resourced backgrounds.

en: Check the MITES website in mid-November 2026, when the 2027 MITES Summer/Semester application opens on the MITES portal
Prepare essays, transcript and activity information
Ask your recommenders early: recommendation requests must be sent by 1 February, and letters are due by mid-February
Submit the online application by 1 February 2027, 11:59 pm PT
Decisions arrive in spring; admitted students attend the residential programme in summer 2027

costs.en: Free. Tuition, on-campus housing and meals are covered by MIT and donors. Students pay only their own travel to and from MIT and personal expenses. No application fee is mentioned.

score_reason: Elite free MIT programme, but restricted to US citizens and permanent residents.

name.ar: برنامج آنسون إل. كلارك للباحثين 2027

duration.ar: 7 أسابيع (من أواخر يونيو إلى أوائل أغسطس)

summary.en: One of the most selective research programmes in the US: just 12 students spend seven weeks doing real research with Texas Tech faculty. No programme fee, free room and board, and a $750 stipend.
summary.ka: აშშ-ის ერთ-ერთი ყველაზე შერჩევითი კვლევითი პროგრამა: მხოლოდ 12 მოსწავლე შვიდი კვირის განმავლობაში ნამდვილ კვლევას ატარებს Texas Tech-ის პროფესორებთან. საფასური არ არის, საცხოვრებელი და კვება უფასოა, და $750-იანი სტიპენდია.
summary.ar: من أكثر برامج البحث انتقائية في الولايات المتحدة: 12 طالباً فقط يقضون سبعة أسابيع في بحث حقيقي مع أساتذة جامعة تكساس التقنية. بلا رسوم، مع سكن وطعام مجانيين ومكافأة 750 دولاراً.

about.en:
The Anson L. Clark Scholars Program is an intensive seven-week summer research programme at Texas Tech University for twelve highly qualified rising high-school seniors and recent graduates. Each scholar joins a faculty research group in a field of their choice (sciences, engineering, mathematics, humanities, business and more) and works on a real project, ending with a written research report.

Alongside research, scholars attend weekly seminars, social activities and weekend programming, and live together on campus. With only a dozen places nationwide, it is one of the most selective pre-college programmes in the United States and carries real weight in university admissions.

There is no participation fee: on-campus housing, meals and weekend activities are provided, and each scholar receives a $750 stipend after submitting a successful research report. The programme is open only to US citizens and permanent residents.

en: Only 12 scholars selected: extremely prestigious
Free housing and meals plus a $750 stipend
Real one-to-one research with Texas Tech faculty in many disciplines

eligibility.en: US citizens or permanent residents, at least 17 years old by the programme start date, graduating high school in 2027 or 2028 (i.e. participating the summer before senior year or right after graduation). No exceptions.

en: Read the 2027 research areas and essay prompts on the Clark Scholars website (you can draft essays before the portal opens)
Create an account when the application opens on 2 January 2027
Upload unofficial transcripts and SAT/ACT (or at least PSAT/PreACT) score reports
Enter three recommenders (at least two teachers); they complete an online questionnaire by the deadline
List your top five activities, pay the $25 fee and submit by 15 February 2027, 11:59 pm CT

costs.en: No programme fee. On-campus room, meals and weekend activities are provided; $750 stipend on completion of the research report. Students pay the $25 application fee, travel, personal and medical expenses.

score_reason: Free, prestigious and well documented for 2027, but US citizens/PRs only and only 12 places.

summary.ka: ექვსკვირიანი პრაქტიკული კვლევა Stony Brook-ის უნივერსიტეტის ლაბორატორიაში სკოლის მიერ ნომინირებული მე-11 კლასელებისთვის, რომელიც კვლევითი პოსტერით სრულდება. სწავლის საფასური არ არის; მიიღება განმცხადებლების 5%-ზე ნაკლები.
summary.ar: ستة أسابيع من البحث العملي داخل مختبر في جامعة ستوني بروك لطلاب الصف الحادي عشر المرشحين من مدارسهم، تنتهي بملصق بحثي. بلا رسوم دراسية، ويُقبل أقل من 5% من المتقدمين.

about.en:
The Simons Summer Research Program gives academically talented high-school juniors the chance to do real research in science, mathematics or engineering at Stony Brook University. Simons Fellows are matched with faculty mentors in chemistry, computer science, geosciences, marine science, neurobiology and more than a dozen other departments, join active research teams, learn laboratory techniques and pursue a question of their own.

The 2027 programme runs 28 June to 6 August 2027 and ends with a research poster symposium. Prior research experience is not required, but the programme is highly selective: 1,864 students applied in 2026 and fewer than 5% are admitted. Many fellows go on to become Regeneron Science Talent Search scholars.

Applicants must be nominated by their school (up to three students per school) and rank three preferred mentors or research areas. There is no tuition, but residential participants pay for housing and meals.

en: Real lab research with Stony Brook faculty mentors
No tuition or programme fee
Strong track record of Regeneron STS scholars

eligibility.en: High-school juniors (11th grade) at the time of application, US citizens or permanent residents only (no visa holders), at least 16 by the programme start, and nominated by their school.

en: Ask your school to submit a nomination by 29 January 2027 (max. three students per school)
Open the online application after it is posted on 15 November 2026
Upload your transcript, write short responses (max. 300 words each, no AI-generated text) and rank three mentors from the mentor list
Pay the $75 fee (waivers for financial hardship) and submit by 5 February 2027, 11:59 pm EST
Teacher recommendations are due 12 February 2027; decisions are emailed in early April

costs.en: No tuition or programme fee. Residential participants pay for housing and dining; commuters pay their own transport and meals. Application fee US$75 (waivers available).

score_reason: Tuition-free and prestigious with full 2027 dates, but US citizens/PRs only and requires school nomination.

summary.en: An eight-week biomedical research internship in Stanford Medicine labs for US high-school juniors and seniors, with no cost to selected students. Selection strongly favours Bay Area students.
summary.ka: რვაკვირიანი ბიოსამედიცინო კვლევითი სტაჟირება სტენფორდის მედიცინის ლაბორატორიებში აშშ-ის მე-11 და მე-12 კლასელებისთვის; შერჩეული მოსწავლეებისთვის უფასოა. უპირატესობა ენიჭება სან-ფრანცისკოს ყურის რეგიონის მოსწავლეებს.
summary.ar: تدريب بحثي طبي حيوي لمدة ثمانية أسابيع في مختبرات ستانفورد للطب لطلاب الصفين الحادي عشر والثاني عشر في الولايات المتحدة، مجاني للمقبولين. تُفضَّل طلبات طلاب منطقة خليج سان فرانسيسكو.

about.en:
SIMR places about 50 high-school students in Stanford Medicine research labs for eight weeks. Students choose an institute or research area (such as immunology, stem cells and regenerative medicine, neuroscience, cancer biology, cardiovascular medicine, bioengineering or genetics/genomics), work on a project under a mentor, attend lectures by Stanford faculty, and present a poster at the end of the summer.

The tentative 2027 dates are 7 June to 29 July 2027. The programme exists to give students, especially those from groups under-represented in medicine and science, early exposure to biomedical research.

There is no cost for selected students and a few need-based stipends are available, but housing is not provided: participants must live with a parent or relative, and selection heavily favours local Bay Area students. Only US citizens or permanent residents living in and attending high school in the US may apply.

en: Eight weeks in a Stanford Medicine lab with a research mentor
No programme cost; limited need-based stipends
Poster session and lectures from Stanford faculty

eligibility.en: Juniors or seniors (class of 2027 or 2028), aged 16+ by June 2027, living in and attending high school in the US, and US citizens or green-card holders. Local (Bay Area) students are strongly favoured; students must arrange housing with a family member.

en: Read the SIMR mission and FAQ pages carefully, especially the housing rule
Download the programme information and application when posted on 18 December 2026
Choose your preferred institutes/research areas and write the essays
Pay the $50 fee (waived for family income under $80,000) and submit by the late-February 2027 deadline

costs.en: No cost for selected students. Application fee US$50 (waivers available). No housing or transport provided; a very limited number of need-based stipends exist.

score_reason: Free Stanford lab research, but US-only, local-favoured and no housing.

summary.en: Canada's best-known pre-university STEAM and entrepreneurship programme: a month living at a Canadian university, tackling a real-world design challenge with peers. Open to international students at a higher fee.
summary.ka: კანადის ყველაზე ცნობილი წინასაუნივერსიტეტო STEAM და მეწარმეობის პროგრამა: ერთი თვე კანადურ უნივერსიტეტში ცხოვრება და რეალური პრობლემის გადაჭრაზე გუნდური მუშაობა. ღიაა საერთაშორისო მოსწავლეებისთვისაც, უფრო მაღალ ფასად.
summary.ar: أشهر برنامج كندي ما قبل الجامعة في مجالات STEAM وريادة الأعمال: شهر من الإقامة في جامعة كندية والعمل مع الأقران على تحدٍّ تصميمي واقعي. مفتوح للطلاب الدوليين برسوم أعلى.

about.en:
Shad is a 27-day summer programme hosted on partner university campuses across Canada (for example Calgary, Western in London, and others; the list varies by year). Students in Grade 10 or 11 live in residence and learn across five interdisciplinary areas, from AI, robotics and biomedical engineering to design, entrepreneurship and the humanities, through lectures, labs, field trips and a team design-and-entrepreneurship challenge. A virtual option runs 5–30 July 2027.

With over 20,000 alumni, Shad is a respected name for Canadian university and scholarship applications, and its alumni network is a big part of the value. The 2027 on-campus programme runs 4–30 July 2027.

Fees for 2027 are CA$7,875 (live-in) or CA$3,975 (virtual) for Canadian citizens and permanent residents, with up to the full fee covered for low-income families. International students can apply but pay CA$12,475 (live-in) or CA$6,750 (virtual) and are not eligible for Shad's financial aid.

en: A month living on a Canadian university campus with top students
Team challenge combining STEAM and entrepreneurship
Large alumni network; CA$5 million in fee assistance yearly for Canadians

eligibility.en: High-school students currently in Grade 10 or 11 (Secondaire IV or V in Quebec). Open to all nationalities; non-Canadians (no citizenship, PR or refugee status) pay the international fee and cannot receive Shad financial aid.

en: Create an account on Shad's application page (free to apply)
Optionally submit by 8 November 2026 for an early decision and a guaranteed top-10 campus choice
Complete the written responses, activity information and references
Submit by 6 January 2027, 11:59 pm ET; decisions arrive in the first week of February
If admitted, pay a CA$750 deposit; the balance is paid in two instalments

costs.en: 2027 fees: domestic CA$7,875 live-in / CA$3,975 virtual (need-based assistance up to the full fee); international CA$12,475 live-in / CA$6,750 virtual, no aid. The live-in fee covers programme, residence, meals and activities; travel is extra.

score_reason: Open now to all nationalities with confirmed 2027 dates, but expensive for international students with no aid.

duration.ar: مرحلة المقترحات من ديسمبر 2026 إلى مارس 2027؛ يقضي الفائزون نحو أسبوعين في CERN أو DESY أو ELSA أواخر سبتمبر 2027

deadline_note: Official: proposals accepted from December 2026 until 12 March 2027, 23:59 CET. Winners announced in June; experiments in late September 2027.

summary.en: A free worldwide competition in which teams of secondary-school students design a particle-physics experiment; the winners travel to CERN, DESY or ELSA to run it on a real beamline. All costs for the winning teams are paid.
summary.ka: უფასო მსოფლიო კონკურსი, რომელშიც საშუალო სკოლის მოსწავლეთა გუნდები ნაწილაკების ფიზიკის ექსპერიმენტს გეგმავენ; გამარჯვებულები CERN-ში, DESY-ში ან ELSA-ში მიემგზავრებიან, რომ ის ნამდვილ ამაჩქარებელზე ჩაატარონ. გამარჯვებული გუნდების ყველა ხარჯი დაფარულია.
summary.ar: مسابقة عالمية مجانية تصمم فيها فرق من طلاب المدارس الثانوية تجربة في فيزياء الجسيمات، ويسافر الفائزون إلى CERN أو DESY أو ELSA لإجرائها على خط حزمة حقيقي. جميع تكاليف الفرق الفائزة مغطاة.

about.en:
Beamline for Schools (BL4S) invites teams of high-school students from anywhere in the world to propose an experiment that uses a particle beam. Teams (with a teacher or adult coach) write a proposal of up to about 1,000 words and a one-minute video explaining their idea, from testing detectors to measuring particle properties or materials science.

Proposals for the 2027 edition can be submitted from December 2026 until 12 March 2027. CERN scientists shortlist the best and the winning teams are announced in June; they then work with physicists to plan their experiment and spend roughly two weeks in late September 2027 at CERN (Geneva), DESY (Hamburg) or ELSA (Bonn), with travel, accommodation and meals fully covered.

Since 2014 thousands of teams from over 100 countries have entered. Even non-winning teams can earn special prizes (up to 50 teams), video awards and participation certificates. It is completely free and a superb project for a school physics club.

en: Run your own experiment on a real particle-accelerator beamline
Free to enter; winners' travel, accommodation and meals fully covered
Open to secondary-school teams worldwide, with online events from November 2026

eligibility.en: Teams of secondary-school students (typically at least five members) from any country, supervised by a coach aged 18+ (usually a teacher). Students must be at least 16 to travel to CERN/DESY/ELSA if they win; younger students may take part in the proposal stage. Proposals are written in English.

en: Form a team and find a coach (teacher or adult mentor)
Attend the online information events from November 2026 and read the 2027 invitation and proposal guidelines
Write your experiment proposal and record the short video
Submit via the BL4S website between December 2026 and 12 March 2027 (23:59 CET)
Winners are notified in June 2027 and travel in late September 2027

costs.en: Free to participate. For winning teams BL4S covers travel, accommodation and three meals a day.

score_reason: Free, open worldwide, confirmed 2027 deadline and a once-in-a-lifetime prize at CERN.

about.en:
UNIQ is the University of Oxford's flagship widening-participation programme, running since 2010 and working with more than a thousand students a year. Participants attend a regional event in spring, then a one-week subject-specific residential in Oxford in late June or July (Monday to Friday), living in a college, attending lectures and tutorials, and experiencing student life.

After the residential, UNIQ provides sustained online support from August to December to help participants make a competitive Oxford application, including help with admissions tests and interviews. Subjects span sciences, engineering, maths, medicine, humanities and social sciences.

The programme is completely free. It prioritises students with good grades from backgrounds under-represented at Oxford, but is open only to students at UK state schools; international students are not eligible.

en: One week living and studying in an Oxford college, all costs covered
Wide range of subjects with Oxford tutors
Ongoing support for the Oxford application, admissions tests and interview

eligibility.en: Students at UK state schools in Year 12 (England and Wales), Year 13 (Northern Ireland) or S5 (Scotland) with strong grades. Priority for students from under-represented backgrounds (e.g. low-income, first-generation, care-experienced, areas with low progression to university). Not open to international or independent-school students.

en: Register on the UNIQ website to be told when the 2027 application opens in December 2026
Check the selection criteria and choose a course
Complete the online application (only through the UNIQ website)
Submit before the January 2027 deadline; late applications are never accepted
Accept your place within a week of the February decision email

costs.en: Completely free: accommodation, meals, academic programme and travel to Oxford are covered.

score_reason: Excellent free Oxford programme, but limited to UK state-school students and 2027 dates not yet posted.

summary.en: A highly selective residential research programme where grade 10–11 students work in University of Iowa labs alongside faculty mentors and earn university credit. Open to international students, with aid covering up to 95% of the fee.
summary.ka: მაღალი კონკურსის რეზიდენციული კვლევითი პროგრამა, სადაც მე-10–11 კლასელები აიოვას უნივერსიტეტის ლაბორატორიებში პროფესორებთან ერთად მუშაობენ და საუნივერსიტეტო კრედიტს იღებენ. ღიაა საერთაშორისო მოსწავლეებისთვის; დახმარება საფასურის 95%-მდე ფარავს.
summary.ar: برنامج بحثي داخلي شديد الانتقائية يعمل فيه طلاب الصفين العاشر والحادي عشر في مختبرات جامعة آيوا مع مرشدين من أعضاء هيئة التدريس ويحصلون على ساعات جامعية. مفتوح للطلاب الدوليين، مع مساعدات تغطي حتى 95% من الرسوم.

about.en:
SSTP is a five-and-a-half-week research programme run by the University of Iowa's Belin-Blank Center for gifted students. Each participant joins a faculty research group and completes a project, ending with a research poster. Research departments for 2027 range from biochemistry, genetics, neuroscience and microbiology to chemical, civil, electrical and mechanical engineering, business analytics, psychology and even religious studies.

Students live on campus, attend classes and events designed to build research and academic skills, and earn three semester hours of University of Iowa credit. The 2027 programme runs 16 June to 23 July 2027 and students must commit to the whole period.

The programme fee is US$7,500 (room, board, materials, activities and credit included). Merit- and need-based aid can cover up to 95% of costs and is applied for after acceptance. International students are welcome: they need proof of English proficiency on acceptance and a US visa; the centre buys their health insurance and provides transport from Cedar Rapids airport.

en: Real research in a university lab with a faculty mentor
Three semester hours of University of Iowa credit
Open to international students; aid up to 95% of costs

eligibility.en: High-school students in grades 10–11 at the time of application, from any country. SAT or ACT scores are required. International students must show English proficiency (residency in some countries satisfies this) if admitted and obtain a student visa. Students may attend SSTP only once.

en: Read the 2027 research areas and programme expectations
Open the online application from 15 December 2026 and enter your details
Pay the US$95 fee (waivers on request) and nominate two referees (one academic, one character)
Write two essays (research interests; motivation and career goals, max. 750 words each), upload your transcript and SAT/ACT scores
Submit everything, including references, by 16 February 2027; decisions on 1 April 2027

costs.en: Programme fee US$7,500 including room, board, materials, activities and three credit hours; travel and incidentals extra. Need- and merit-based aid up to 95% of costs, applied for after admission. Application fee US$95 (waivable).

score_reason: Confirmed 2027 dates, open to internationals, real research and generous aid.

summary.en: A residential programme at Bentley University where 14–17-year-olds complete an original computational or AI research project, chosen with Stephen Wolfram and guided by expert mentors. International students are accepted and need-based aid covers up to 90%.
summary.ka: რეზიდენციული პროგრამა Bentley-ის უნივერსიტეტში, სადაც 14–17 წლის მოსწავლეები ასრულებენ ორიგინალურ გამოთვლით ან ხელოვნური ინტელექტის კვლევით პროექტს, რომელიც სტივენ ვოლფრამთან ერთად შეირჩევა. საერთაშორისო მოსწავლეები მიიღებიან, საჭიროებაზე დაფუძნებული დახმარება 90%-მდე ფარავს.
summary.ar: برنامج داخلي في جامعة بنتلي يُنجز فيه طلاب بعمر 14–17 عاماً مشروعاً بحثياً أصيلاً في الحوسبة أو الذكاء الاصطناعي يُختار بالتعاون مع ستيفن وولفرام وبإشراف مرشدين خبراء. يُقبل الطلاب الدوليون وتغطي المساعدات حتى 90%.

about.en:
The Wolfram High School Summer Research Program is an intensive two-and-a-half-week residential programme that turns motivated high-school students into computational researchers. After workshops and lectures on the Wolfram Language, computational thinking and AI, each student carries out a personal research project, selected in collaboration with Stephen Wolfram and supported by a mentor, and publishes it at the end. Past projects range from cellular automata and molecular modelling to linguistics and image processing.

The 2027 programme takes place at Bentley University in Waltham, near Boston, from 28 June to 17 July 2027. Coding experience is not required: admissions value problem-solving, creativity and maturity. Strong participants can continue in the Wolfram Emerging Leaders Program or join the teaching team.

The fee is US$6,500 including room, board and a year of access to Wolfram technologies. Need-based aid on a sliding scale covers up to 90% of programme costs (not travel or the US$500 deposit). International students are welcome but must obtain their own visa.

en: Original, publishable research project chosen with Stephen Wolfram
No coding experience needed; strong mentoring
International students accepted; aid up to 90%

eligibility.en: Students aged 14–17 (exceptional 13-year-olds sometimes accepted; nobody who turns 18 during the programme). Any STEM background; open to international students, who must obtain any necessary visa.

en: Complete the online application when it opens in early November 2026, including short responses on past projects and alumni projects
Request financial aid within the application if needed (no aid requests after 23 April)
Do the video interview with the Admissions Director
Apply by 18 January 2027 (Early Decision, results by 15 Feb) or 15 March 2027 (Regular, results by 23 April)
Pay the US$500 deposit to confirm; the balance is due by 10 May 2027

costs.en: US$6,500 including room, board and a one-year Wolfram licence; includes a non-refundable US$500 deposit. Need-based aid up to 90% of programme costs; travel not covered.

score_reason: Open worldwide, confirmed 2027 dates and fees, generous aid and a real research output.

about.en:
Pioneer pairs high-school students with professors from research universities for a rigorous, independent research project in almost any field: mathematics, physics, computer science, biology, economics, psychology, history, philosophy and more. Students work in small seminar groups and one-to-one with their professor, and finish with an original research paper evaluated to university standards.

The programme is fully online, so students can take part from any country. Students with passing grades earn four transferable college credits awarded via Pioneer's partnership with Oberlin College, and outstanding papers can be published in the Pioneer Research Journal.

Tuition is US$7,465 (plus, in some cases, a lab/materials fee of up to 2%). Pioneer has awarded about US$14.9 million in need-based scholarships since 2014; these are available where family need can be verified or through partner schools and non-profits. Applications for 2027 are open now.

en: One-to-one research with a university professor, fully online
Four transferable college credits via Oberlin College
Need-based scholarships up to full tuition

eligibility.en: Current high-school students (grades 9–12) from any country. Strong academic record and English ability for university-level reading and writing; standardised tests optional.

en: Attend an online information session (optional)
Register on the Pioneer application portal and choose research areas
Upload an unofficial transcript and invite your counsellor to support at least a week before submitting
Submit by 13 December 2026 for the Spring-through-Summer term, or by the Summer-term deadline announced in January 2027
Request a need-based scholarship in the application if needed

costs.en: Tuition US$7,465 (possible lab/materials fee up to 2%). Need-based scholarships available where need can be verified; full-scholarship students pay a refundable deposit.

score_reason: Accessible worldwide with aid, but expensive and a commercial programme; deadline very soon.

about.en:
The Research Mentorship Program places high-achieving high-school students with a UCSB mentor for an intensive, individual research project in fields across the sciences, engineering, social sciences and humanities. Students attend research-methods classes and the GRIT talks lecture series, write a research paper and present their findings at a closing symposium, earning UC credit.

The 2027 programme runs 14 June to 31 July 2027, beginning with a short virtual component (14–17 June). Students may live in a UCSB residence hall with other pre-college students or commute.

It is a paid programme: 2026 costs were US$5,675 for commuters and US$13,274 for residential students (tuition plus housing and meals); 2027 pricing is published in early December. A limited number of need-based scholarships are available, with priority for California residents. International students are welcome and do not need TOEFL/IELTS scores.

en: One-to-one mentored research and a final symposium
University credit from UC Santa Barbara
No English test needed for international applicants

eligibility.en: High-school students in grade 10 or 11 (outstanding 9th graders case by case) with a weighted academic GPA of at least 3.80. International students welcome; no TOEFL/IELTS required. Students cannot take other courses or programmes during RMP.

en: Attend an RMP information webinar (optional)
Open the online application from 15 December 2026
Upload your full high-school transcript and any AP score reports, and write the required statements
Indicate scholarship interest in the application if needed
Pay the US$75 fee and submit before the 2027 deadline (around early March)

costs.en: 2026 guide: commuter US$5,675 (US$75 application fee + US$5,600 tuition); residential US$13,274 (adds US$7,599 housing and meals). 2027 prices published in early December 2026. Limited need-based scholarships, priority to California residents.

score_reason: Respected, open to internationals with 2027 dates; expensive and limited aid.

about.en:
The Summer Research Academies are a shorter, group-based introduction to university research. Students choose a research track (tracks change yearly and cover areas such as engineering, biology, psychology, data science and the social sciences), attend lectures, labs and discussions, then design and carry out a group project, ending with a presentation. They earn four UC Santa Barbara credits.

The 2027 programme runs 25 June to 23 July 2027, starting with a welcome event and two-day academic intensive. It is a good stepping stone for younger students (grades 9–11) who are not yet ready for the one-to-one Research Mentorship Program.

Costs in 2026 were US$3,475 for commuters and US$9,874 for residential students; 2027 pricing is released in early December. International students may apply without TOEFL/IELTS scores.

Accepts students from grade 9
International applicants welcome, no English test

Pay the US$75 fee and submit before the 2027 deadline

about.en:
King's College London's Pre-University Summer School gives students in their final three years of high school a taste of studying at a leading London university. Each course lasts one week and mixes lectures, seminars, discussion groups, simulations and guest speakers; students can take one, two or three courses across four sessions in July 2027.

2027 sessions: 5–9 July (Business Management; Science, Technology & Engineering), 12–16 July (Accounting & Finance, Economics, International Relations, Media & Creative Industries, Neuroscience), 19–23 July (Business Management, Data Analytics for Business & Finance, International Relations, Law, Science, Technology & Engineering) and 26–30 July (Accounting & Finance, Business Management, English Language & Culture, International Relations, Law, Neuroscience). Students get a King's certificate of participation and a social programme.

It suits international students who want to test a subject before applying to UK universities. Residential students live in single en-suite rooms at Stamford Street Apartments with 24-hour supervision, breakfast and dinner. No scholarships are advertised.

about.en:
Warwick's Pre-University Summer School (PRESS) is an 11-day residential programme on the university's campus near Coventry. Students choose one of six 'taster' courses taught by Warwick staff: Arts, Culture and Society; Economics and Finance; Business, Management and Marketing; Health, Medical and Life Sciences; Science and Engineering; or Social Sciences. Each mixes lectures, seminars, a guest speaker and personal-development workshops.

The programme also includes sessions on applying to UK universities, a social and cultural programme and trips, including a day in Oxford. The 2027 school runs 20–30 July 2027. Warwick is a top-10 UK university, and the course is a gentle, well-supervised first experience of UK campus life.

The £5,500 fee is all-inclusive (10 nights' accommodation, breakfast and dinner, teaching, social programme and trips). No specific English test is required. No scholarships are advertised.

about.en:
Sciences Po's on-campus Pre-College Programme introduces secondary-school students to the disciplines and methods of one of Europe's leading social-science universities. Over two and a half weeks (35 contact hours) all students take the same core courses in the social sciences, joined by smaller tutorial groups that teach the Sciences Po method, plus master classes and an elective. The 2027 programme runs 3–20 July 2027 in central Paris.

For those who cannot travel, Sciences Po also runs an online two-week World Climate Negotiations Bootcamp, where students role-play international climate negotiations and learn international-relations theory.

Admission is selective but rolling, with decisions about a month after a complete application. 2026 fees were €6,000 (on campus: courses, materials, local transport; no accommodation) and €2,000 (online), plus a €50 application fee. Sciences Po offers no scholarships.

about.en:
Harvard's Secondary School Program (distinct from its two-week Pre-College Program) lets motivated high-school students enrol in college-level Harvard Summer School courses taught by Harvard or visiting faculty, alongside college students and adults from around the world. Students earn a letter grade and a Harvard transcript.

In 2027 there are two four-week sessions (14 June–8 July and 12 July–5 August; one 4-credit course, about 20 courses to choose from) and a seven-week session (21 June–6 August; one or two courses from more than 200, spanning molecular biology, psychology, computer science, economics, law, entrepreneurship and more). Students can live on campus, commute or study online, with activities, tutoring and a writing centre.

2027 costs range from US$4,180 (one online or commuting course) to US$9,260 (4-week residential) and US$15,980 (7-week residential with two courses), plus a US$75 application fee. Need-based aid is available, but for residential students it is limited to US citizens and permanent residents; Harvard sponsors visas for international residential and commuting students.

200+ courses; 4- or 7-week options, residential or online

about.en:
Summer Challenge is Boston University's two-week, non-credit pre-college programme for students entering their sophomore, junior or senior year. Each student takes one small, discussion-based seminar (past topics have included creative writing, engineering, entrepreneurship, psychology, public health and international relations), then joins daily activities, workshops and trips around Boston.

2027 residential sessions are 20 June–2 July, 11–23 July and 25 July–6 August (commuter sessions start the next day). It is a low-pressure way for younger students to try US campus life before committing to longer programmes such as BU's three-week Academic Immersion or six-week RISE.

In 2026 the total charge was US$5,245 residential (tuition, housing, meals and activities) or US$3,989 commuter, plus a US$75 application fee. BU states that no financial aid is available for Summer Challenge. International students can apply; BU publishes separate guidance for them.

en: Short, two-week introduction to US college life
Small seminars in a subject of your choice
Three 2027 session dates to fit school calendars

about.en:
Exeter Summer is Phillips Exeter Academy's century-old summer programme, bringing more than 600 students from over 40 countries and 30 US states to its campus in New Hampshire, an hour north of Boston. Classes use the Harkness method: around a dozen students and a teacher discuss the material at an oval table, so preparation, listening and contributing matter more than grades.

In the Upper School (for students who have completed grades 9–12) students choose three courses across many disciplines, or one of two clusters: the Charles J. Hamm '55 Leadership Program or the Engineering Design Lab. Afternoons bring sports and performing arts, with dorm life, weekend trips and campus events. The 2027 programme runs 5 July to 5 August.

It is a strong option for international students who want an authentic US boarding-school experience and practice in seminar-style learning, which prepares them well for US universities. Need-based aid exists but only for US applicants.

Students from more than 40 countries

about.en:
Andover Summer Session is the summer programme of Phillips Academy, one of the oldest and most selective boarding schools in the United States. Students choose from more than 70 academic courses and intensive institutes across the humanities, sciences, mathematics, computer science and the arts; the Upper School is for rising 9th–12th graders and the Lower School Institute for rising 7th–8th graders.

The 2027 session runs 29 June to 1 August 2027 near Boston. Boarding students live in dorms with peers from around the globe and take part in athletics and activities; add-ons include college counselling, study skills and SAT/PSAT/SSAT preparation, and new for 2027 a L.E.A.D. leadership class.

Tuition for 2027 is US$11,500 (Upper School boarding) plus a US$400 activities fee; day students pay US$3,250–6,500. Andover lists financial-aid information on its tuition page. Students need basic English proficiency (around TOEFL iBT 80, IELTS 6.0 or Duolingo 95–100, though scores need not be submitted).

Afternoons and evenings include sports, swimming, hiking and campus activities; optional add-ons (for a fee) include SSAT prep and a boarding-school application course. The programme has an international student body.

about.en:

Each student joins one seminar taught by Notre Dame faculty; 2027 topics include AI and Global Business, LEAD-AI, Global Issues: Violence and Peace in the Modern Age, Inequality in America, The American Experiment: Liberty for All?, and The Power of Investing. Seminars combine discussion, readings, service and reflection on what leadership means.

Students may earn one transferable college credit. Session I runs 19–30 June and Session II 10–21 July 2027.

If admitted, the university pays tuition, housing and meals; students cover a US$75 application fee, a US$150 enrolment fee and travel. about.en:
Summer Scholars offers rising juniors and seniors an intensive two-week preview of college academics. Each student takes one small course taught by Notre Dame faculty; 2027 options include Cryptography: From Classical to Quantum-Secure Systems, Engineering and Inventing the Future, Exploring the World of Chemistry, Life Sciences (ecology and cancer biology), Object Design and Prototyping, Climate Change, Law, Psychology, Public Policymaking, Public Speaking and Debate, Film Production, Journalism, Business and Entrepreneurial Immersion.

International students take part through iLED (International Leadership, Enrichment and Development), which adds sessions on leadership, innovation, entrepreneurship and cultural competence, a day of service, and Q&A sessions with Notre Dame admissions. Students may earn one college credit, so international participants need an F-1 visa.

The 2027 cost is US$5,200 in total (US$75 application fee, US$300 enrolment fee and US$4,900 tuition, room and board, activities and field trips). Some donor grants (e.g. KPMG for the Accounting course) can cover programme costs for qualifying students via the Financial Aid Request Form.

During two weeks in the summer between junior and senior year, students sample every major branch (aerospace, mechanical, chemical and biomolecular, civil, environmental, electrical, computer engineering, computer science and geological sciences) through informal lectures by faculty and practising engineers, team design projects, programming, lab and facility tours, and field trips.

Constructor University (the former Jacobs University Bremen) is an English-speaking private research university in northern Germany. Its Talent School runs a 12-day international Summer Camp in which high-school students choose two of ten university-level courses: Mathematics & Modeling, Programming & Algorithms, AI & Robotics (building and training a robot with reinforcement learning), Chemistry & Research, Biology & Research, Physics & Research, Neuroscience & Psychology, Innovation & Entrepreneurship, Economics & Investments, and Probability & Data Science.

The 2027 camp runs 9–20 July 2027. Students live on the Bremen campus with mentors, mixing lectures, tutorials and team projects with sports, culture nights and excursions to Bremen and Hamburg. Past cohorts have included more than 40 nationalities.

The programme price of €5,100 includes tuition, accommodation, meals, excursions, domestic transport and supervision, with €500 off for applications before 31 December 2026. Flights, visa and health insurance are extra. It is a good way to test studying in Germany in English.

about.en:
CERN's Particle Physics Course for High-School Students is a research-based online course created by CERN's Physics Education Research team. Its 16 chapters (about four hours in total) use short videos and self-grading quizzes to introduce fundamental questions such as 'What is a particle?', the Standard Model, the Higgs boson, the LHC and detectors such as ATLAS, antimatter, dark matter and dark energy, and how scientific inquiry works.

The course is free, self-paced and open all year to students aged 14–18 anywhere. Subtitles can be auto-translated into any language, and it includes do-it-yourself experiments and further reading. Students who complete all chapters and quizzes receive a digital certificate.

It is an ideal first step for students considering physics or engineering, and good preparation for CERN's Beamline for Schools competition. In September 2026 the course moved to the OpenLearn Create platform (previous learners must retake quizzes there).

Established in 1990, Smith's Summer Science and Engineering Program (SSEP) is designed for high-school students with strong interests in science and engineering. Students take one lab-based course per two-week session with Smith faculty in the life sciences, physical sciences and engineering; recent courses include Designing Intelligent Robots and a sport and exercise psychology lab course. Those who stay both sessions take two courses.

The 2027 sessions are 3–16 July and 18–31 July. Students live on campus at Smith, one of the largest US women's colleges, and get a taste of college life with activities and weekend trips. College credit is not offered.

2026 tuition was US$4,985 per two-week session or US$9,970 for both (2027 rates coming soon). Need-based tuition assistance is available to a limited number of students (apply by 1 March 2027). International students must submit Duolingo, TOEFL or IELTS scores and apply by 1 March 2027.

Barnard College, the women's college of Columbia University in New York City, runs summer pre-college institutes taught by Barnard faculty and expert instructors. The NextGen Leadership Institute pairs leadership development with a course in Scientific Exploration, Literature & Performing Arts or Global Humanities; the Health & Society Institute explores public health and medicine; and the Athena Summer Innovation Institute (Session I only) focuses on innovation and entrepreneurship. Students can join one or both three-week sessions: 28 June–16 July and 19 July–6 August 2027.

Learning happens through discussion, hands-on projects and the city itself, with residential or commuter options. A separate Pre-Baccalaureate Program lets older students take a real undergraduate course for credit (2027 details to be announced).

In 2026 the three-week institutes cost US$8,160 (commuter, with weekday lunches) or US$10,771 with on-campus housing and full dining. Limited need-based aid exists but international applicants are not eligible for it.

about.en:

Internship-track students spend 40 hours a week on a project designed by a faculty member, postdoc or graduate-student mentor in fields such as astronomy, biology, biomedical engineering, chemistry, computer science, electrical and computer engineering, neuroscience and physics. Practicum-track students follow a structured course with lectures and group research (2026 subjects were Computational Neurobiology and Data Science; 2027 options are announced in December).

All students join weekly workshops on academic and professional skills and present at the closing poster symposium. The 2027 programme runs 27 June to 6 August (residential) and 28 June to 6 August (commuter).

In 2026 RISE cost US$10,735 residential or US$6,415 commuter, with limited need-based aid applied for inside the application. It is open only to US citizens and permanent residents.

about.en:
IE University's Pre-Tracks are five immersive two-week summer programmes that let students in their final years of high school test a degree path before applying: Pre-STEM, Pre-Business, Pre-Law, Pre-Global Affairs and Pre-Design. Taught in English by IE faculty at the IE Tower campus in Madrid, they use real cases, team challenges and presentations, with classmates from around the world and a programme of cultural and social activities.

2027 intakes: 27 June–9 July and 11–23 July (Pre-Global Affairs runs only in the second intake). For younger students (14–17), IE also runs a Pre-University Discovery Summer Program split between Segovia and Madrid.

The fee for both the Pre-Tracks and Pre-University programmes is €5,900, covering the academic programme, full-board accommodation and transport within Madrid/Segovia. No scholarships are advertised. It is especially relevant for students considering IE, Esade or other Spanish and European business, law or tech degrees.

about.en:
Stanford Summer Session lets high-school sophomores, juniors and seniors study alongside Stanford and visiting university students for eight weeks. Students choose from 130+ regular courses across disciplines (computer science, engineering, mathematics, psychology, economics, writing and more), take at least 8 units if residential, and receive grades and an official Stanford transcript.

The 2027 session runs 19 June to 15 August 2027. Beyond class, students get lab and research-centre visits, access to libraries, sports facilities and maker spaces, residential life and a free College Essay Cohort to draft a college essay.

It is expensive: Stanford's per-unit tuition is US$1,505; published estimates start at US$18,771 for residential students (8 units, housing and meals) and US$8,226 for high-school commuters (minimum 5 units). Tuition grants are limited to undergraduate and graduate students, so high-school students should expect to pay in full. International students are welcome and need an F-1 (or other study) visa.

eligibility.en: Current high-school sophomores, juniors or seniors at the time of application, at least 16 at the start of the programme and no older than 19 by the last day; not matriculating to Stanford as a first-year. International students welcome (proof of English if needed; F-1 visa required).
